findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

The allowlist takes precedence over sensitive-field masking, and it includes `key`. An ordinary short credential supplied under that name therefore survives unchanged. The verified inline MCP path computes sanitization flags but passes the original input at `inline-agent-loop-tools.ts:328–353`; `durable-interaction-handler.ts:181` then persists this projection. Although the generic renderer hides the field, the new durable snapshot retains its plaintext value. Apply credential-name masking to remote-tool inputs before allowing display fields, while preserving browser keyboard-key inputs explicitly.
findings.title: Not done: sensitive key values are hidden in durable snapshots

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

Shortening the string before redaction can remove the context identifying a retained secret. For example, a long command can place a quoted `password=` assignment in the omitted middle while the last 1,000 characters retain part of its credential value. Neither subsequent redaction pass can recognize that suffix. On the verified raw-input inline MCP path (`inline-agent-loop-tools.ts:351`), it is persisted through `durable-interaction-handler.ts:181` and can appear in the command preview (`permission-tool-input-format.ts:130–150`). Redact the complete value before applying the head/tail limit.
findings.title: Not done: redact secrets before shortening prompt details

findings.body:
chunk 1/2:

The named end-to-end test replaces the application's permission-approval surface, then implements binding, callback claiming and decision construction itself at lines 176–200. It never delivers the tap through the real Telegram callback handler (`callback-handlers.ts:737–793`). Consequently, broken native callback routing or decision resolution would leave this test green. This violates the required boundary rule, “Fake only third-party services at their edge.” Drive the actual channel approval and callback paths, faking Telegram's external API only.
findings.title: Not done: permission-prompt-shape exercises real channel callbacks

stop.reason: Owner: keep it simple, like Claude Code. Narrow to the three open findings: run the one secret rule over the full text before any shortening, mask every credential-named field (key included) with no allowlist exceptions, store only the shown text, and drive the e2e tap through the real Telegram handler
